description: SandboxShellTool's restricted mode rejected shell operators from a denylist that omitted newline and carriage return, so 'allowed_cmd\nrm -rf ...' passed the allowed=[...] / readonly=True prefix check and the second line ran as a command.
notes: CVE-2026-113663, fixed 1.1.1. Allowlist/denylist bypass in an agent shell tool. Follow-up bef9a8efc0 (1.1.2, GHSA-42mf) reworks the filter again: deferred.

description: The async Jobs API installs its router with no auth middleware or dependency, so any caller who can reach it submits agent jobs, reads results and cancels or deletes jobs.
notes: Fix adds an opt-in JobsAPIKeyMiddleware (PRAISONAI_JOBS_API_KEY).

description: try_get_class_from_dynamic_module resolved auto_map classes for the Transformers backend without honouring trust_remote_code, so a model repo's auto_map ran remote code at init.
notes: trust_remote_code bypass chain, 2 of 3.

description: api_endpoint again selected the serde from the client-controlled media type, so application/vnd.bentoml+pickle bodies were deserialized with pickle (unauthenticated RCE).
notes: Pickle-serde chain, fix 2 of 2: regression/bypass of CVE-2024-2912 (kbc-ghsa-hvj5-mvw9-93j3). Fix is a merge commit from a private fork.

description: ContextExpression substituted string ContextVariable values into the expression with a raw f-string (no repr/escaping) and then eval()ed it; the AST allow-list ran on the template, not on the substituted expression, so a quote in any variable value breaks out into arbitrary Python.
notes: Fixed in 0.13.2. The commit message cites GHSA-9fvw-gr53-m7fw (not resolvable via the API); repo advisory 35w5 describes the same eval sink. Variable values arrive from tool output, APIs or persisted state, hence untrusted-data-store.

description: The CSV Agent component hardcoded allow_dangerous_code=True, so the LLM's Python tool runs whatever a prompt-injected model emits on the Langflow host.
notes: Same pattern at line 123 (build_agent); one row kept. Sibling of the Flowise CSVAgent chain.

description: executeJavaScriptCode merged caller-supplied nodeVMOptions over the safe defaults, so a flow could re-enable builtin require (child_process) and escape the NodeVM sandbox.
notes: Flowise NodeVM chain, 1 of 2; next escape is kbc-ghsa-wg86-r78f-74mp.

description: MediaConnector fetched user-supplied image/audio URLs with redirects enabled, so the --allowed-media-domains restriction was bypassed by a redirect to an internal address.
notes: SSRF chain, fix 1 of 2. Second bypass (URL-parser differential) is kbc-ghsa-qh4c-xf7m-gxfc.

description: ENABLED_TOOLS, toolset and read-only filters are applied only in _list_tools_mcp; tools/call dispatches from the full registry, so any client that knows a tool name can call a tool the operator disabled (the fix adds _call_tool_mcp with the same authorization check).
notes: The vulnerable behaviour is an absent call-time check; the locator is the listing-only filter that should also guard dispatch.

description: hf_chat_template rendered the model's chat_template (fetched from the Hugging Face hub) in a non-sandboxed Jinja2 Environment, so a malicious tokenizer_config gives SSTI/RCE.
notes: Fix is a merge commit; switches to ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment.

description: Inspector's connection settings (transport, serverCommand, serverArgs) were read from window.location on every route including /oauth/callback, so a malicious MCP server's OAuth redirect to the callback with transport=stdio&serverCommand=... switched Inspector to stdio and ran an arbitrary local command.
notes: v1 line fix (1.0.3). OAuth-callback confused-deputy into stdio exec; fix ignores query params on /oauth/callback.

description: The base64 segment of an uploaded csvFile data URI was interpolated unescaped into a Python string literal executed by Pyodide, so a crafted data URI breaks out and runs code as root.
notes: Flowise CSVAgent chain, 2 of 3. GHSA-vmv7 describes the same line-161 injection; one sink, one fix commit, so one row. Fix removes CSVAgent/AirtableAgent.

description: The Playwright web loader validated the URL once and then let the browser resolve DNS itself, so a rebinding domain reached internal services.
notes: Open WebUI SSRF chain, 2 of 2 (time-of-check/time-of-use on DNS).

description: get_instance_fn imported and executed any module path named in proxy config (e.g. post_call_rules), so a config writer could load arbitrary code.
notes: Fix commit title ('test fix post call rules') is misleading; it adds the validation to types_utils/utils.py.

description: mcp-server-git's git_init tool created repositories at any filesystem path, ignoring the --repository confinement; the fix removes the tool.

OAuthProxy issued its own JWTs with a fixed audience derived from base_url and ignored the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter, so a token minted for one MCP server is valid at any other server sharing the proxy's keys/base URL (token reuse across MCP servers).
notes: Fix #2764 builds the JWTIssuer in set_mcp_path() with the real resource URL and validates the client's `resource`. Audience-binding class (MCP spec token passthrough).

description: web_crawl validated only the first URL, then httpx followed redirects automatically, so a public page can 302 the crawler to loopback/metadata addresses.
notes: Three advisories on one sink. Incomplete-fix chain: GHSA-qq9r-63f6-v542 / GHSA-8f4v-xfm9-3244 (1.5.128) added the first-URL check; these bypass it via redirect and unchecked fallback.

description: Python generated by the LLM was checked by a regex denylist and run in Pyodide, which can reach Node; a prompt injection makes the model emit a bypassing script and get host RCE.
notes: Flowise CSVAgent chain, 3 of 3 (same fix commit as kbc-ghsa-4j8x-x6v7-w9rq, different sink). Model-mediated attacker: CHAINLAB input. GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2 (validator homoglyph bypass) belongs to this sink family but its fix predates this commit (NFKC already present), so it is not added.

description: The redirect-blocking SSRF hook was attached only in the header-PAT branch of _get_fetcher; the basic-auth and OAuth branches build fetchers without it, so an attacker-controlled Jira/Confluence URL can redirect requests to internal hosts.
notes: Incomplete fix of GHSA-7r34-79r5-rcc9 (fix 5cd697d). Fix adds attach_ssrf_hook=True to the basic and OAuth branches and a session-level hook in the client constructors.

description: The multimodal shared-memory cache trusted client-forgeable SHM handles and deserialized the referenced bytes with pickle.loads in the worker, giving RCE from a public request.
notes: Fix authenticates SHM handles; the pickle.loads sink itself stays.

description: confluence_upload_attachment resolved the caller-supplied file_path with os.path.abspath() and opened it with no workspace confinement, so a prompt-injected or authenticated client reads any server file (e.g. /proc/self/environ) and exfiltrates it as a Confluence attachment.
notes: Five advisories (same sink, one fix commit). GHSA-6cr4 and GHSA-p6hp are 'incomplete fix of GHSA-xjgw-4wvw-rgm4' (the download-side write was fixed in 0.17.0, the upload-side read was not). Fix is the 0.22.0 omnibus commit.

description: The Browser Server's WebSocket Origin check uses re.match() with an unanchored chrome-extension://[a-z0-9]{32} pattern, so any origin merely starting with that prefix passes and a web page can hijack the browser-automation socket.
notes: Patch bypass of GHSA-8x8f-54wf-vv92 (the advisory that introduced the origin check).

description: Every tool opened the repository and ran git against it with the repository's own .git/config trusted, so core.fsmonitor, hooks, filter drivers, gpg.program etc. in a cloned/unpacked repo run arbitrary programs as the server user even on read-only calls such as git_status.
notes: Config-exec wave, 1 of 6 (head of chain). Fix adds harden_repo(): GIT_CONFIG_COUNT overrides + per-repo driver blanking. The five rows below are bypasses of this hardening. Pattern: git wrapper that does not neutralise repository-controlled config.

description: Mustache (and f-string) prompt templates resolved names with getattr() on arbitrary Python objects, so an attacker-authored template could traverse object attributes and leak data.
fetchToken sent stored client credentials to whatever authorization server the MCP server's metadata named, without binding them to the issuer they were registered with.
LocalPythonExecutor allowed reaching forbidden submodules through indirect attribute access (getattr on an authorized module), escaping the import allowlist to run arbitrary code.

download_attachment's validate_safe_path() defaults base_dir to os.getcwd(), so a target path inside the working directory root (e.g. an importable app module) is accepted; overwriting it gives code execution.
notes: Explicit bypass of the 0.17.0 fix for GHSA-xjgw-4wvw-rgm4 (CVE-2026-27825). The same omnibus commit adds the refusal to write into the CWD root.

description: The /prompts/test endpoint rendered caller-supplied dotprompt content with an unsandboxed Jinja2 Environment, giving server-side template injection to code execution.
notes: A second advisory for the same endpoint, GHSA-xqmj-j6mv-4862 (CVE-2026-42203), has no commit ref; not merged into this row because the fix link is unconfirmed.

description: A remote MCP App's ui/open-link request made the client window.open() an attacker URL without noopener, giving the page a handle/sessionStorage access to steal the proxy auth token; because the sandbox is same-origin with the proxy, the missing-Origin check let it then call the stdio launch API (RCE).
notes: v1 line fix (1.0.3). Same commit adds a Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin refusal in server/src/index.ts originValidationMiddleware; locator is the noopener/open-link step of the chain.

description: The code printer emitted identifier names through recast's literal printer and JSON.stringify at print time; tampering with shared builtins (JSON.stringify) or crafting names injected source into the generated 'name in data ? data : global' switch, executing attacker code outside the sandbox.
notes: Same bundle commit as kbc-ghsa-hw8v-xxg5-vvvx but a different file and sink (code-printer injection; fix adds rawStringLiteral and safeStringify captured at load).

description: mcp-remote passes the authorization_endpoint URL from an untrusted MCP server's OAuth metadata straight to open(), which shells out; a crafted URL runs OS commands on the client host.
notes: OSV lists 607b226 (username/password escaping) as the fixed commit; the primary fix introducing sanitizeUrl() is 783bf86. Both ship in 0.1.16.

description: MCP auth skipped LiteLLM key validation whenever any Authorization header was present (treated as an OAuth2 passthrough token), so an arbitrary bearer string reached MCP tools.
notes: MCP-gateway token-passthrough class (charter: R&D territory).

description: NemotronVL hardcoded trust_remote_code=True when building the vision model from config, overriding the user's explicit opt-out and executing the model repo's code.
notes: trust_remote_code bypass chain, 3 of 3. Same fix also patches kimi_k25.py (same pattern, one row kept).

description: The Qwen3-Coder tool-call parser converted parameter values of unknown type with eval() on model output, so a prompt-injected model response executes Python inside the vLLM server.
notes: The advisory references the commit that introduced the parser (4594fc3b, #21396); the actual fix is 4e51fa8c (#23266, 'Do not use eval() to convert unknown types'), found via the file's commit history. Model-mediated attacker: CHAINLAB input.

description: The Inspector proxy accepted unauthenticated requests (no token, no Origin check) and spawned query.command via StdioClientTransport, so any web page could run local commands (CSRF / DNS rebinding).
notes: Fix is a merge commit; vuln sha is its first parent.

description: AgentServer accepts an auth_token in its config but never checks it: the /events and /publish routes serve any caller, exposing agent activity and letting them publish events.
notes: Earlier fixes in the same family: GHSA-f292-66h9-fpmf (A2U SSE, 4.5.115).

description: The git diff handler interpolated a request-supplied file path into a double-quoted shell command (git show "rev:path"), allowing command injection in the runtime.
SqliteStore search concatenated filter keys into json_extract() SQL, so attacker-controlled filter keys injected SQL.
`praisonai serve ... --api-key K` stored the key in config but never installed any middleware, so the served agent endpoints stayed unauthenticated even though the operator set a key.
notes: Three advisories, one missing enforcement. Chain: GHSA-6rmh-7xcm-cpxj (legacy API server auth disabled, 4.6.34) -> these (4.6.58) -> GHSA-892r-p3jq-jp24 (AgentOS still unauthenticated, 4.6.59).

description: harden_repo did not stop lazy fetching: a repository with promisor-remote configuration made git fetch missing objects, and the fetch ran a program the config names.
notes: Config-exec wave, 3 of 6: fix sets GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and refuses promisor remotes on older git.

description: The vendored Nemotron-VL config resolved vision_config.auto_map with get_class_from_dynamic_module, loading remote code from a model repo even with trust_remote_code=False.
notes: trust_remote_code bypass chain, 1 of 3 (with kbc-ghsa-2pc9-4j83-qjmr and kbc-ghsa-7972-pg2x-xr59). Fix deletes the config copy.

description: PythonREPLComponent ran user/agent code via langchain PythonREPL with a weak globals 'sandbox' and no allow_custom_components gate, giving authenticated RCE.
notes: Fix also patches components/tools/python_repl.py (same sink, one row kept).

description: harden_repo only blanked filter/merge drivers from the top repository's config; a checked-out submodule's own config and .gitattributes still selected a driver that ran during git_add/git_checkout/git_diff.
notes: Config-exec wave, 6 of 6: fix adds _submodule_drivers() and diff.submodule=short; two follow-up commits complete it.

description: validate_url relied on ipaddress.is_global, which treats NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) addresses as global, so any user could reach internal services and cloud metadata through the web loader.
notes: Open WebUI SSRF chain, 1 of 2; DNS-rebinding bypass is kbc-ghsa-4v28-j6q3-5m4r.

description: FastMCP HTTP servers on localhost had DNS-rebinding protection (Host/Origin validation) off by default, so a web page could reach an unauthenticated local MCP server.

The Python task-runner AST validator blocked dangerous attributes and regex-checked literal format strings, but allowed bare str.format / format_map attribute access and aliasing, so format-string attribute traversal reached blocked internals and escaped the Python sandbox.
notes: Bundle 2.x commit #31173 (fixed 2.22.4/2.21.8/1.123.48); the fix adds bare-format attribute rejection in the validator and a FormatGuardTransformer in the executor.

description: The SQLite checkpointer's list() metadata filter interpolated filter keys into SQL (json_extract path), enabling SQL injection.

harden_repo read the repository config once, but git_merge writes the working tree: a merged branch can add a file that a config [include] now pulls in, defining filter/merge drivers that were never blanked and then run on the next git command.
notes: Config-exec wave, 5 of 6: fix routes every tree-writing command through _rewrite_tree(), which re-runs harden_repo afterwards. TOCTOU on hardened config.

description: OAuthProxy.authorize() redirected straight to the upstream IdP for any dynamically registered client with no user consent step, so an attacker's client could ride the victim's existing IdP session (confused-deputy account takeover).
notes: Fix #2056 'Prevent confused deputy attacks in OAuth proxy' adds the consent screen, CSRF token and redirect-URI warnings. Confused-deputy chain, 1 of 2: consent added here, bypassed by kbc-ghsa-rww4-4w9c-7733 (consent not bound to the browser at the IdP callback).

description: dumps() did not escape user dicts containing 'lc' keys, so LLM-influenced fields round-tripped through loads() as constructor/secret markers; the Reviver returned os.environ secrets.
isDeniedIP compared the parsed address against the deny list without unwrapping IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:127.0.0.1), so the SSRF protection was bypassed.
notes: Incomplete-fix class: bypass of Flowise's earlier SSRF deny-list hardening.

description: In the documented multi-user streamable-http deployment the middleware lets requests with no user identity through; the handler then falls back to the operator's global Atlassian credentials, so unauthenticated network clients can invoke every tool.
notes: Fix adds a 401 for identity-less requests unless ALLOW_GLOBAL_CRED_FALLBACK is set. GHSA-wrhw (critical, AtlassianOpaqueTokenVerifier accepts any token) cites the same commit but its diff does not touch the verifier: deferred, see notes.

description: Webhook-triggered flow execution defaulted to no authentication, so anyone who knows a flow id can run the flow (and any code components in it).
VectorSQLDatabaseChain eval()'d every value returned by the LLM-generated SQL query, so a prompt injection that shapes the query result executed Python.
The workspace containment check used abspath instead of realpath, so a symlink inside the workspace escapes it for agent read/write tools.
notes: Same family as GHSA-gcq3-mfvh-3x25 (code agent tools fail open w/o workspace).

description: The Jira upload_attachment tool reads a caller-supplied file_path from the MCP server's filesystem (abspath only, no confinement) and uploads it to Jira, the read-side twin of the download write fixed earlier.
notes: Jira-side sink of the same upload-read family as the confluence row. vc25/f6pj/mrq8/wv8v name both services; 2xj6 reaches the same upload code via update_issue's attachments parameter. Mapping of the multi-service advisories to the Jira sink is by reading the fix diff.

description: Resource-scoped auth decorators (@auth.on.threads(actions=[...])) ignored actions= and always registered the handler for '*', so a narrow handler shadowed the broader fallback handler that enforced ownership and the authorization check never ran for other actions.
notes: Fixed in langgraph-sdk 0.4.4. Design-level authz bug in the framework's own auth API (the application code is correct as written).

description: download_integration exec()'d an f-string built from module and class names, so attacker-controlled names executed arbitrary code.

The Git node's clone validated the target path and then cloned into it later, so swapping a directory for a symlink between check and use (TOCTOU) planted a repo in the community-nodes directory, which n8n loads as code on the next restart.
notes: Bundle 2.x commit #33793 (fixed 2.30.1). Fix clones into an unguessable staging dir and renames into place. Part of the Git-node incomplete-fix history (GHSA-57g9, GHSA-rcv6 not pinned, see notes file).

description: A malicious MCP server's authorization URL (e.g. javascript:) was navigated to without scheme validation, giving XSS in the Inspector client, which can drive the proxy to execute commands.
RecursiveUrlLoader fetched crawled links with only a startsWith() origin check and no private-address validation, so a page could steer it to internal URLs.

The Recipe server's api-key/JWT middleware falls open (call_next) when auth is enabled but no key or secret is configured, so a non-localhost bind passes the CLI check yet serves unauthenticated requests.
notes: Fail-open default; fix returns 503 'misconfigured'.

description: get_secret decoded Google KMS encrypted secrets with eval(), so a crafted secret value (environment/config) executes Python in the proxy.
notes: Fix is a merge commit; vuln sha is its first parent.

description: The expression variable polyfill treated ArrowFunctionExpression as 'do nothing', so a concise arrow body that is a bare identifier (() => process) was never routed through the data context and reached host globals, escaping the expression sandbox into command execution.
notes: Fix commit is the 'Bundle/2.x' release-branch commit #34680 (n8n ships security fixes in bundle commits; the file diff isolates this sink). Fixed 2.31.5/2.32.1. First of an expression-sandbox chain: GHSA-hw8v and GHSA-6xcw (2026-09) are later bypasses of the same sandbox with different holes.

description: FileMemory uses user_id as a directory name unsanitised, so '../' sequences write memory files outside the memory root.
notes: Related earlier advisory: GHSA-766v-q9x3-g744 (memory state leakage and path traversal in multi-agent context handoff, 1.5.115).

description: git_merge could trigger automatic maintenance (git gc --auto), which honours gc.recentObjectsHook from the repository's own config and runs it; HARDENED_CONFIG did not disable maintenance.auto / gc.auto.
notes: Config-exec wave, 4 of 6: fix adds maintenance.auto=false and gc.auto=0 to HARDENED_CONFIG. The locator is the hardening list that lacks the entry.

description: server-filesystem checked allowed directories with a bare startsWith(), so /allowed_evil passes for /allowed; the same commit fixes the symlink check a few lines below (GHSA-q66q-fx2p-7w4m).
notes: Two advisories, one validatePath() sink and one fix commit: kept as one row. ID pairs (gh API 2026-11-25): GHSA-hc55-p739-j48w = CVE-2025-53110 (colliding path prefix, this row's primary advisory and locator); GHSA-q66q-fx2p-7w4m = CVE-2025-53109 (symlink handling, same commit). Cite this row as CVE-2025-53110.

description: Skill archive installation joined tar member names onto the staging dir without checking the result stayed inside it and used the archive-supplied skill name as a path before validating it, enabling arbitrary file write and (via rmtree of final_dest) delete.
notes: Fixed 1.1.0. Two sinks in one function (write at line 99, rmtree before validation ~118); one row, the extraction write.

description: validate_url_for_ssrf trusts urlparse().hostname, so http://localhost\@evil.com/ validates as evil.com while requests/WHATWG connect to localhost; the fix rejects a backslash in the authority.
notes: Parser differential between the SSRF gate (urlparse) and the executor (requests/urllib3). Bypass of the SSRF guard added for GHSA-7r34-79r5-rcc9.

description: ray.data.read_webdataset's default decoder unpickled .pickle/.pkl (and torch.load'ed .pt) members of the dataset shards, so reading an attacker-supplied dataset runs code.
After the first Mooncake fix, the metadata sockets still bound tcp://* and decoded (src_ptr, length) with ZMQ recv_pyobj(), i.e. pickle.loads on unauthenticated network input.
notes: Incomplete-fix chain, fix 2 of 2 (bypass of the CVE-2025-29783 fix, kbc-ghsa-x3m8-f7g5-qhm7). The fix moves to struct-packed multipart and binds to the configured host.

description: StatelessProcessGroup (used by PyNcclPipe KV transfer) started its TCPStore listening on all interfaces and exchanged objects with pickle.loads(store.get(...)), so a network peer can plant a pickle and get RCE; the fix binds the listening socket to the configured host.
notes: The deserialization sink (recv_obj pickle.loads, line 192) is unchanged by the fix; the fix is the network exposure at the TCPStore creation, so the locator is the store creation and sink_class is 'other'.

description: The service endpoint picked the request deserializer from the client's Content-Type, including the pickle serde, so an unauthenticated request body was unpickled (RCE).
notes: Pickle-serde chain, fix 1 of 2; reopened as kbc-ghsa-33xw-247w-6hmc.

description: replay_request_dump.py loads request-dump files with pickle.load, so a planted dump file executes code when an operator replays it.
notes: PR #20904 also is referenced by the critical SGLang ZMQ pickle advisories (GHSA-jx93-g359-86wm, GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58), but it only fixes this script; those sinks are unchanged at the fix commit, so they are not in the corpus (see notes).

description: PrototypeSanitizer visited assignments and member access but had no visitClassBody, so a class field with a reserved name (or a template-literal key) rebound the sanitizer's own reserved variables and the expression escaped the sandbox to code execution.
notes: Bundle 2.x commit #37586 (fixed 2.38.2/2.37.7/1.123.76). Incomplete-fix chain: a further bypass of the hardening after kbc-ghsa-gv7g-jm28-cr3m. Locator is the visitor list where visitClassBody was missing.

description: A workflow 'include' of a recipe directory exec_module()s that directory's tools.py without the PRAISONAI_ALLOW_LOCAL_TOOLS opt-in that guards the other autoload paths, so a crafted recipe runs arbitrary Python at load.
notes: Incomplete fix of GHSA-xcmw-grxf-wjhj (tool_override autoload gate, 4.6.32): sibling load path.

description: The ReadFile agent tool read whatever path the model supplied, exposing arbitrary server files to a prompt-injected agent.
Streamable HTTP served requests for an existing session id without checking the caller is the principal that created it, so one user could drive another user's session.
The WriteFile agent tool wrote to whatever path the model supplied (no base-path confinement), so a prompt-injected agent could overwrite arbitrary files (RCE).
notes: Same fix commit also fixes ReadFile (kbc-ghsa-j44m-5v8f-gc9c).

description: Agno eval()'d the field_type string from a tool's user-input schema, so model- or user-supplied field types executed arbitrary Python.
BaseCache defaulted to JsonPlusSerializer(pickle_fallback=True), so cache entries were unpickled on read: RCE for anyone who can write the cache backend.
File-typed inputs given as a URL string were downloaded server-side with httpx with no destination check, so any caller could make the server fetch internal URLs.
notes: Same commit guards the request-body URL path at line 166.

description: The Completions API decoded client-supplied prompt_embeds with torch.load; a crafted sparse tensor bypasses weights_only checks and corrupts memory (DoS, potential RCE).
notes: Fix gates embeds behind --enable-prompt-embeds / --enable-mm-embeds; a follow-up hardening is GHSA-mcmc-2m55-j8jj (no commit ref, not added).

description: The driver-listing regex needed at least one character in the driver name (filter\..+\.), so a driver with an empty name ([filter ""] clean = ...) was never blanked and still ran a program.
notes: Config-exec wave, 2 of 6: bypass of the harden_repo fix (kbc-ghsa-6hqx-gqrx-c5r2). Vuln SHA e1d154ee is shared by the 11-18 bypass rows (pm7p, 87qg, h2g3, 9vjp, 8wv7); locators differ. The fixes are stacked branches v2/fix/ghsa-*, each advisory with its own commit.

description: The MCP HTTP-stream transport's Origin allowlist uses startswith(), so http://localhost.attacker.com is accepted and a web page can drive the unauthenticated local MCP server.
notes: Same prefix-match bug class as the Browser Server and MCP SSE origin advisories.

description: RunGptLLM eval()'d each streamed SSE event from the model server, so a malicious or spoofed server response executed code in the client.

validate_opened_repo (the fix for GHSA-w766) accepted any git dir that equalled the allowed repo's own and ignored objects/info/alternates and linked-worktree git dirs, so an in-repo repository could still read objects from outside --repository.
notes: Confinement chain, 2 of 2: incomplete fix of kbc-ghsa-w766-5x43-whvw. Same commit a4a43ac fixes GHSA-6hqx (separate row, different sink). Merged by PR #5514 (1629bb33).

description: Inspector opened the OAuth authorization_endpoint chosen by the remote MCP server via npm open v10, which on Windows/WSL embeds the URL in a PowerShell double-quoted string, so a $(...) subexpression in the URL executes code while connecting.
notes: v2 line fix 2.12.0 (bump open to v11, restrict to http(s)). Follow-up f7e0377ab8 opens the serialized URL rather than the raw input. Same sink class as kbc-ghsa-6xpm-ggf7-wc3p (mcp-remote).

description: load_from_url checked the media-domain allowlist on urllib's urlparse() hostname while the request library parsed the URL differently, so a crafted URL passed the check and fetched an internal host.
notes: SSRF chain, fix 2 of 2: bypass of the CVE-2025-6242 fix (kbc-ghsa-3f6c-7fw2-ppm4). Fix switches to urllib3 parse_url so check and fetch agree.

description: Legacy load_prompt() followed template_path / example paths from a prompt config with no containment, reading arbitrary files.
DiskKnowledgeStore confined virtual paths with str.startswith on the resolved root, so a sibling directory sharing the root's name prefix (/data/root-evil vs /data/root) passed the containment check.
notes: Classic startswith-prefix containment bug; the fix is Path.is_relative_to. Fixed 1.1.0.

description: The OAuth client accepted authorization-server metadata without validating its issuer, so a malicious MCP server could point it at an attacker AS and receive the client's credentials.
LangChain.js load() revived attacker-shaped 'lc' secret objects from serialized data and read the named environment variable, enabling secret extraction.
The jobs webhook URL validator swallows DNS resolution errors (except gaierror: pass), so an unresolvable-at-check, resolvable-at-use hostname (rebinding) bypasses the private-IP rule.
notes: Chain: GHSA-8frj-8q3m-xhgm (4.5.128, first webhook SSRF) -> GHSA-rjvw-7vvw-549v (DNS rebinding, 4.6.59) -> this fail-open. The file has the same pattern twice (two models); the first is used.

description: hf_model_weights_iterator loaded .bin checkpoint files with torch.load without weights_only, so a malicious model repository executes code when vLLM loads it.
notes: Bypassed for PyTorch < 2.6 (GHSA-ggpf-24jw-3fcw, fixed by a dependency bump, not added). Attacker is a malicious model, not a network client.

description: requireBearerAuth accepted tokens issued for another service because it never compared the token's resource/audience with the server's own.
notes: v1.x branch fix.

description: POST /api/v1/validate/code had no authentication and passed the body to validate_code, which exec()s decorators/default args, giving unauthenticated RCE (CISA KEV).
notes: validate_code chain, 1 of 2: auth added; the exec stays and is reopened for authenticated users by kbc-ghsa-v798-mcc6-2m3m.

description: Validating a tool result against a server-supplied output schema resolved remote $ref URLs, so a malicious MCP server could make the client fetch arbitrary URLs.

_handle_idp_callback loaded the transaction and issued the client authorization code without checking that the browser arriving at the callback is the one that approved consent; a lured victim whose IdP skips its own consent page completes the attacker's flow.
notes: Incomplete-fix chain, 2 of 2 (bypass of the consent screen from kbc-ghsa-c2jp-c369-7pvx). Fix #3201 adds a signed consent-binding cookie verified in the callback. A follow-up CSRF double-submit fix is #3519 (8fdb3cc2). VARIANT seed: consent/state bound to the flow but not to the browser.

description: validate_code still exec()'d each import/function definition of submitted code (decorators and defaults run at definition time), so any authenticated user got RCE.
notes: validate_code chain, 2 of 2 (after CVE-2025-3248). Two advisories, one sink and one fix commit: kept as one row. Fix stops executing code in validate_code.

description: The web server served index.html with the API token injected on routes outside the /api origin check and never validated the Host header, so a DNS-rebinding page could fetch / same-origin (no Origin header), read the token and then the stored OAuth secrets.
notes: Incomplete-fix chain: second bypass of CVE-2025-49596 (v2 line, fixed 2.12.0); fix adds a Host allow-list on every request.

description: The WebSocket server transport accepted the handshake with no Host/Origin validation, enabling cross-site WebSocket hijacking of a local MCP server.
mcp-server-git git_add passed tool-supplied paths to repo.index.add(), staging files outside the repository boundary.
notes: Fix is a merge commit; vuln sha is its first parent.

description: FastMCP's OpenAPI provider substituted tool-call path parameters into the upstream URL unencoded, so ../ or @host values redirected requests (path traversal / SSRF).
The public-flow build endpoint accepted a caller-supplied `data` graph and built it, so an unauthenticated user could submit custom-component code that the server executes.
Bearer auth accepted any token the verifier recognised, including tokens issued for a different resource server (no RFC 8707 audience check), enabling token replay across services.

JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER was applied only when the JQL did not already contain 'project =' and the tool-supplied filter replaced the configured one, so a caller names a forbidden project in its own JQL and reads it.
notes: Two sinks, one advisory: this row is the Jira half; the Confluence half is the -b row.

description: CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER was skipped when the CQL already contained 'space = ', so a caller names a forbidden space in its own CQL and reads it.
notes: Confluence half of GHSA-w66g (see the Jira row, suffix-less id).

description: open_repo validated only the textual repo_path against --repository, then git.Repo(path) followed a nested .git file (gitdir: /outside) so every tool operated on a repository outside the allowed one.
notes: Confinement chain, 1 of 2. Fix adds validate_opened_repo (checks git-dir, common-dir and worktree git actually uses); merged via PR #5333 (b711f8d3). Bypassed by kbc-ghsa-q74p-4wrc-q7w6.

description: MCP stdio server configs (command + args) supplied by a user were spawned as-is, so saving an MCP server config ran an arbitrary OS command on the Langflow host.
notes: Advisory lists two fix commits (PR #12290 and #14036); primary is the #14036 hardening that adds lfx/base/mcp/security.py.

description: Even with the nodeVMOptions fix, the NodeVM sandbox ran without fixAsync and exposed risky external deps, letting custom JS functions escape to the host (elttam).
notes: Flowise NodeVM chain, 2 of 2 (after kbc-ghsa-3769-jgqc-cxm7). Fix also hardens isValidURL in validator.ts (FLOWISE-543/551 in the same commit).

description: Origin validation only rejected a present-but-wrong Origin; with DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH set, a request with no Origin (any non-browser client) reached the privileged stdio launch route without a token, re-opening CVE-2025-49596.
notes: Incomplete-fix chain: bypass of kbc-ghsa-7f8r-222p-6f5g (v1 line, fixed 1.0.3). Fix also makes DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH parse strictly (true/1/yes).

description: The XML node validated a coerced copy (String(options.attrkey)) against __proto__/constructor/prototype but passed the original, non-string option value on to xml2js, so a crafted array value bypassed the earlier prototype-pollution fix and polluted Object.prototype.
notes: Patch bypass (incomplete fix) of GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r; the fix validates the value that is actually used. Bundle 2.x commit #30359. rd_class sandbox-escape is the closest enum value for prototype-pollution-to-RCE.

description: PandasQueryEngine ran LLM-generated code through safe_exec, whose restricted globals still exposed getattr/setattr/iter etc., so a prompt injection reached arbitrary code execution.
JsonPlusSerializer 'json' mode imported and called any module/class named in stored checkpoint data (importlib.import_module), giving RCE from checkpoint contents.
allowed_domains was checked against urlparse().netloc, so a decoy domain in the userinfo part (https://allowed.com:x@evil.com) bypassed the agent's navigation allowlist.
notes: Fix is a merge commit; vuln sha is its first parent.

description: MooncakePipe received KV tensors from the network and decoded them with pickle.loads, so any host that can reach the Mooncake transfer port gets RCE on the vLLM node (ShadowMQ class).
notes: Incomplete-fix chain, fix 1 of 2: this commit swaps the tensor pickle for safetensors but leaves the ZMQ metadata channel on recv_pyobj (pickle) bound to *; that second sink is kbc-ghsa-hj4w-hm2g-p6w5.

description: The spider tool's host guard only blocked literal IPs (inet_aton); hostnames resolving to private addresses passed, so DNS names reach internal services.
notes: New bypass of prior fix 004dcfef (GHSA-q9pw-vmhh-384g).

description: The CSV Agent spliced the user's customReadCSV expression into Python run by Pyodide; the regex validator let read_pickle and class definitions through, giving host RCE via the js bridge.
notes: Flowise CSVAgent chain, 1 of 3 (earlier: GHSA-3hjv-c53m-58jj). Reopened by kbc-ghsa-4j8x-x6v7-w9rq and kbc-ghsa-5xvg-pmgg-3mxr; final fix deletes the node.

description: The Custom MCP env-var denylist (PATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, NODE_OPTIONS) missed npm_config_* variables, so npm_config_yes etc. re-enabled the command execution CVE-2025-8943 had blocked.
notes: Patch bypass of CVE-2025-8943 (incomplete fix). VARIANT seed: denylist of env vars for stdio MCP spawns.

description: InMemoryVectorStore compiled and eval()'d filter lambdas whose AST check allowed dunder attribute access, so a crafted filter escaped to arbitrary code execution.
